commits.message:
fix(markup): settle what a legal plugin tag name is, once (rich-markup-pwr)

A registered plugin name matched as a bare PREFIX of the tag text, and the
failure was silent in both directions.

Registering `table` destroyed every `table.*` built-in: `[table.header]x[/table.header]`
fired the plugin and dropped the `.header` as attributes. The mirror case:
`register("a.b")` succeeded but `[a.b]` could never reach the handler, because
the tag scan stops at the dot.

Both ends wanted the same answer to "what is a legal plugin tag name?" and
neither asked it. There is now one source fragment, anchored two ways:

- MATCH: `^(name)(?=$|[ \t])` — a registered name addresses a plugin only when
  the tag text ends there or continues with the whitespace that introduces
  attributes. `[table.header]` and `[table=x]` fall through to the built-in
  dialect exactly as an unregistered name would.
- REGISTER: `^name$` — a name markup could never address is rejected loudly
  instead of installing an unreachable handler.

The two anchorings are mirrors: every name `register` accepts is one the match
site can reach, and every name it rejects is unreachable.

The six-line hand scanner it replaces is gone; `register` keeps its existing
reserved-name guard, which asked a different question (is this itself a valid
style?) and could not have caught either case.

fix(cells): make chopCells advance on a glyph it cannot split (rich-cells-pfs) (#88)

* fix(cells): make chopCells advance on a glyph it cannot split

chopCells looped forever when a single glyph was wider than the whole
budget, then died with `RangeError: Invalid array length`. It drove the
loop with splitText, which pads to land exactly on the requested column
and hands the unsplittable glyph back untouched — so at a 1-cell budget
`chopCells("日本語", 1)` pushed a padded blank line and a remainder that
never shrank, forever. A terminal reporting a 1-cell width is enough to
reach it, and cc-candybar already floors its fold budget at 2 cells to
route around it.

Drive the loop with cellFitFrom over code-unit offsets instead, taking
`max(fit, nextCodePoint)`: nextCodePoint is always strictly past the
start, so the loop advances by construction rather than by a guard, and
the case where nothing fits force-takes the glyph and lets it overflow
by its own width — the only answer that both terminates and keeps the
text intact. cellFit already documents that its caller must choose
between force-taking and skipping; chopCells now chooses.

Side effect worth naming: chopCells no longer pads. It is a chopping
function, `join("") === input` now holds for every input, and a line
that stops short of a wide glyph is narrower than maxWidth rather than
padded out to it. splitText keeps its padding — that is its job.

* refactor(cells): give the force-take rule one home in cellStepFrom

The "fit what you can, and take one glyph anyway when nothing fits" rule
lived in two places with two spellings: charGreedyWrap in the textarea,
and the loop chopCells just grew. That is not a hypothetical drift risk
— the copies had already drifted, and the drift is the bug the previous
commit fixed: the textarea force-took, chopCells did neither and hung.

Extract cellStepFrom beside cellFitFrom and route both callers through
it. Not exported from the barrel: it is an internal seam between core/
and widgets/, and a new public export is carrying cost plus a
coverage-gate obligation with no consumer asking for it.

charGreedyWrap sheds a dead guard on the way — `if (end === pos) break;`
after nextCodePoint was unreachable, since the loop condition already
guarantees pos < line.length. Its `cap <= 0` guard stays put: a
zero-width row budget is the textarea's concern, not the step
primitive's.

Also scope chopCells' overflow bound to what it can actually promise.
The docstring claimed the only line exceeding maxWidth is one overwide
glyph, which the `maxWidth <= 0` return breaks by handing back the whole
string. Both cases are one rule — a line overflows exactly where the
budget cannot be met — and saying it that way is shorter than the
version that was wrong.

* docs(cells): scope cellStepFrom's advance guarantee to inside the text

The docstring claimed cellStepFrom never returns startCU. At
text.length it does, and correctly so — nothing is left to take, and
that total behavior is what lets both callers drive their loop with no
special case at the end.

The first draft said "for any startCU inside text," which was true; the
pass that shortened it to "never returns startCU" is what dropped the
precondition. Restoring the qualifier and naming the loop shape the
termination argument actually covers.
